attempts.cause: The first evaluator compared one spelling of Docker's no-new-privileges option instead of admitting the engine's exact normalized equivalent.
attempts.corrected_by: Inspection accepts only the two exact semantically equivalent Docker representations and still rejects absence or weakening.

attempts.cause: The first recovery-probe wrapper contained a syntax error and produced no usable product observation.
attempts.corrected_by: The corrected probe was parsed before execution and then completed all nine retained recovery and state scenarios.

attempts.cause: The initial static assertion counted only one runtime-label comparison, allowing the unsafe post-start label-check mutation to survive.
attempts.corrected_by: The validator now requires both independent label-check occurrences; all 24 mutations are rejected.

attempts.cause: The first command named a nonexistent workflow fixture and therefore evaluated no manifest or authority state.
attempts.corrected_by: The existing valid minimal manifest fixture returned approval MISSING, verdict INVALID, and exit 12 before Git or Docker.

attempts.cause: PowerShell parsed the unquoted HEAD^{tree} revision expression as separate syntax, so the aggregate wrapper ended with an unusable revision argument after returning unrelated partial output.
attempts.corrected_by: The tree expression was single-quoted and Git strict object verification was rerun separately; the exact base tree and object graph passed.

attempts.cause: The first additive 29-case run removed the materializer's clean-worktree branch without being rejected because the validator asserted only the Git status call, not its exact fail-closed decision.
attempts.corrected_by: The static validator now requires the exact dirty-worktree rejection branch; all 29 implementation, materializer, and Node-gate mutations are rejected.

attempts.cause: The first focused command omitted the checkout src directory from PYTHONPATH, so tests.test_workflow could not import incidentseal and produced no valid product result. The other fourteen tests in the same wrapper passed.
attempts.corrected_by: The focused suite is rerun with the same explicit checkout PYTHONPATH used by the locked implementation validator.

attempts.cause: The first PowerShell wrapper used the unsupported ConvertFrom-Json -Depth parameter in this host version and then printed misleading PASS labels because the parameter errors were nonterminating.
attempts.corrected_by: The wrapper is rerun with ErrorActionPreference Stop and the supported ConvertFrom-Json invocation before accepting any JSON or JSONL claim.
